Rising river levels this evening may lead to flooding.

Forecast levels may cause flooding to low lying land and roads close to the river from Thursday evening into Friday morning. The main areas of concern are Exebridge, Bolham, Bampton and Tiverton.

We expect the river to remain high into tomorrow morning though no flooding to properties is currently forecast.

Take care and avoid walking, cycling or driving through flood water.

High river levels on Thursday have led to flooding.
Flooding is possible on Thursday 19 November . A lot of rain (21mm) has fallen last night 18/11/2026.
At Langbridge and Alverstone, the river is slowly rising. Flooding is affecting low lying land, roads, cycle tracks and footpaths close to the river. At Sandown the river is high but stable. Flooding of Golf Links Road and Moreton Common Road is ongoing. Ditches around Fort Holiday Park will struggle to drain while river levels are high. Only a small amount of rain is forecast from today 19/11/26 until Saturday 21/11/26. At Alverstone the river will peak by 15:00 19/11/26 and will begin to slowly fall tomorrow 20/11/26. At Sandown the river will remain high over the next 24 hours.
We are monitoring rainfall and river levels and will ensure the river is kept free of reported blockages.
Consider activating any flood protection products you may have. Including in Alverstone.
This message will be updated by 1:00PM on Friday 20 November or as the situation changes.

items.description: The tidal Rivers Bure, Ant and Thurne
items.message: Flooding is possible today, Thursday 19th November, and for the next few days. This is due to tide locking, where high tides restrict normal drainage of the river out to sea. We expect to see high water levels around Potter Heigham, Wroxham boat yards and Ferry Road in Horning. Levels can take several hours to peak compared to published tide tables. We are closely monitoring the situation. Take care and avoid walking, cycling or driving through flood water. This message will be updated by 10am on Friday 20th November, or as the situation changes.
